alsoValidAgainst.name: XMonitor - Telegram Router
alsoValidAgainst.why: Every fixture pins Resolve Caller Authorization, so authorization is decided by pinned data rather than by the environment's own Client Members / Staff rows. The same fixture therefore proves the same graph logic in either environment.

why: Before T2 all four Get Post For * lookups filtered on post_id alone. Post ids are public - they appear in every X URL - so any chat that could reach the bot could hide replies on, snooze, ignore, or place paid SMM orders against any post in the system, including another client's. These fixtures pin that hole shut and are the foundation T4 extends.

design.resolver: One shared step sits between Parse Telegram Message and Route Telegram Intent: Resolve Caller Authorization (Postgres) -> Build Caller Authorization (Code) -> If Caller Known (If). It resolves the caller once into { auth_client_ids, auth_is_staff, auth_is_known }.
design.gates: Each of the four post lookups is followed by an If that passes only when the post exists AND (the caller is staff OR the post's client_id is in the caller's client_ids). All false branches, plus the unknown-chat branch and the /track staff gate, converge on one Build Access Refusal node.
design.failsClosed: Resolve Caller Authorization has alwaysOutputData; an empty result yields no client_ids and is_staff=false, which refuses. Nothing about this design fails open.

invariants: post_not_found and cross_tenant_post MUST produce the SAME user-facing message. Only the post id - which the caller supplied themselves - may differ. Distinguishing them turns the bot into an oracle for probing which post ids exist inside other clients.
The true reason lives in Build Access Refusal's refusal_reason and in the developer alert. It is never in the reply to the user.
A refusal is clean: a friendly message, the callback answered where one exists, and no half-completed side effect.
Order placement is authorized BEFORE any SMMWiz call. The gate sits between the post lookup and Get Comment/Likes Post Tracked User, so it also precedes the OpenAI comment generation.
No fixture in this directory may run /order_comments or a valid /order_likes live. Place Comment Order and Place Likes Order are pinned in every fixture that reaches them.

stagingRows.why: The fixtures here are fully pinned and need no database rows. This script recreates the two synthetic tenants used for the live-resolver acceptance run (resolver and post lookups unpinned), which is how T2 was actually proved and how T4 should re-prove it.
creates: Staff row for the staging operator chat 8677383067
Client Members chat 9900000001 -> tenancy-test-a, chat 9900000002 -> tenancy-test-b
stagingRows.note: The synthetic Clients / Client Members / Tracked Users / Posts rows were removed after the T2 acceptance run. The Staff row was kept - it is the operator's cross-client grant, not test scaffolding.

actors.9900000001: chat A - client member of tenancy-test-a, NOT staff
actors.9900000002: chat B - client member of tenancy-test-b, NOT staff
actors.8677383067: staging operator - Client Members row of house AND a Staff row, so it acts across every client
actors.9900000009: unknown chat - in neither Client Members nor Staff

fixtures.input: callback_query.data=hide_replies:9990000000000000101 from chat B against client A's post

asserts: the callback is answered with 'Post not found.', never with anything that admits the post exists
no reply is queued for hiding

fixtures.input: message.text=/ignore 9990000000000000101 from chat B
message.text=/snooze 9990000000000000101 4h from chat B
message.text=/resume 9990000000000000101 from chat B
message.text=/order_likes 9990000000000000101 25 from chat B

asserts: the refusal happens before any SMMWiz call - SMMWiz has no cancel, so money must be decided first

fixtures.input: message.text=/order_comments 9990000000000000101 from chat B, form comment_amount=10

asserts: the refusal precedes both the OpenAI generation and the SMMWiz call

fixtures.input: message.text=/ignore 9990000000000000999 from chat B - a post id that exists nowhere

asserts: THE ORACLE TEST: normalising the post id out, this message must be byte-identical to cross-tenant-ignore's. If they ever diverge, the bot has become a probe for other clients' post ids.

fixtures.input: message.text=/ignore 9990000000000000101 from chat 9900000009, which is in neither Client Members nor Staff

asserts: an unknown chat is refused BEFORE the route switch, so it can reach no action at all
the developer alert always fires for an unknown chat and carries chat id, name and type so it can be assigned (decision #7)

fixtures.input: message.text=/track @lynnharfoush from chat B, a client member but not staff

asserts: /track is staff-only per decision #3
the message is a plain 'not available' - unlike the post refusals it reveals nothing, because no post id is involved

fixtures.input: callback_query.data=hide_replies:9990000000000000101 from chat A, the post's own client

asserts: the authorized path is unchanged - the gate is transparent when the caller owns the post

fixtures.input: message.text=/ignore 9990000000000000101 from chat A
message.text=/snooze 9990000000000000101 4h from chat A
message.text=/resume 9990000000000000101 from chat A
message.text=/order_likes 9990000000000000101 25 from chat A

asserts: Place Likes Order is pinned to a provider rejection, so the gate is proved open without creating or charging an order

fixtures.input: message.text=/order_comments 9990000000000000101 from chat A, form comment_amount=10, confirmation='Do nothing'

asserts: the confirmation is pinned to cancel, so the gate is proved open without placing an order

fixtures.input: callback_query.data=hide_replies:9990000000000000202 from the operator chat against client B's post

asserts: a Staff chat acts across every client without holding a Client Members row for that client - this is what stops the operator breaking the moment client #2 exists

fixtures.input: message.text=/ignore 9990000000000000101 from the operator chat against client A's post
message.text=/track client:house @lynnharfoush from the operator chat

asserts: T5: a staff /track names the client explicitly and the upsert receives that client_id
the T2 staff gate still admits the caller before any of it

fixtures.input: message.text=/track @lynnharfoush -- no client: token

asserts: T5 refuses rather than guessing an owner; the pre-T5 sole-active-client fallback is what this replaces
nothing is deactivated, so a mistyped /track cannot empty a client list

fixtures.input: message.text=/track client:nosuchclient @lynnharfoush

asserts: an unknown slug is named back to the caller with the valid slugs -- safe only because /track is staff-only
no row is touched before the client resolves

fixtures.input: message.text=/track client:house @lynnharfoush with the upsert pinned to the blocked shape (RETURNING matched no row)

asserts: a blocked ownership takeover deactivates NOTHING -- succeeded_ids is empty so the deactivate statement no-ops
the caller is told the account is owned elsewhere instead of being told success
regression guard for the defect T5 introduced: the deactivate used to run first and empty the target client list

note: Every fixture in tests/n8n/telegram-router-risky-pins/ must also still pass unchanged after T2. They all run as chat 8677383067, which is a Staff row, so is_staff short-circuits the owner check and their pinned post rows - authored before T1 and carrying no client_id - are never consulted. If one of them ever starts failing, the resolver is rejecting something it should allow.
